title: Lay a robot axis's two cables into its cable carrier and snap every crossbar shut
instruction: Lay both cables side by side into the cable carrier, grey on the far side, without crossing, and snap every crossbar shut.
context: Every linear axis, gantry and robot track built for a robot cell carries its motor and encoder cables in a cable carrier (energy chain). Filling it is a manual step of building the axis, repeated whenever a cable is replaced: the chain is laid out straight, each link's crossbar swung open, the cables laid in side by side in a fixed order, and each crossbar swung back and pressed until its catch snaps. What goes wrong: a cable left riding a side plate so its crossbar cannot latch, cables crossed inside the chain (they chafe through in service), a crossbar left resting on its catch that springs open on the first stroke. It is hard because two limp cables must be lifted over the side plates and lowered side by side into a 25 mm channel, then twelve 1 g hinged crossbars swung over and pressed home at 30.5 mm pitch. Unlike #7 (one cord pressed into an open channel), the skill tested is the snap-latching crossbars over two cables kept in order.
setup: All real size. Metres; x forward, y left, z up; origin midway between the arm bases (0,+-0.305); table top z=0.7475. (1) Cable carrier, igus E2 mini B15.025.038.0 (snap-open on the outer radius; Igumid G nylon, black): 12 links, pitch 30.5 mm, 366 mm long, inner width 25 mm, outer width 36 mm, inner height 17 mm, outer height 23 mm, bend radius 38 mm, about 0.15 kg. It lies straight along y, openable side up, centreline at x=0.170, fixed end at y=+0.183, moving end at y=-0.183, lying on the table with its links on their straight stops. Fixed-end mounting bracket screwed to the bench (y +0.183 to +0.205); moving-end bracket loose (y -0.183 to -0.205). Per link: 5.5 mm side plates 20 mm tall, a fixed 3 mm bottom crossbar, and an openable crossbar (31.5 x 10 x 3 mm, 1.1 g) hinged on the far side plate (hinge at x=+16.5 mm, 21.5 mm above the table); all twelve stand open at 100 deg on their stops, leaning away from the robot. Closing: the bar's free end is pressed past a sprung catch on the near side plate (45 deg lead-in, 2.5 mm overhang, spring 0.9 N preload rising to 1.7 N), about 3 N at the free end; a closed bar sits flush with 0.8 mm of play under the catch, an unlatched one rests on the catch 4.1 mm proud. (2) Strain-relief plate (steel, 40 x 16 x 3 mm) screwed to the bench 100 mm behind the fixed end, centre (0.170, 0.283). (3) Grey servo-motor cable, 7 mm PVC, 560 mm, 42 g, tie-wrapped to the plate at (0.176, 0.283), 6.8 mm above the table. (4) Orange encoder cable, 5 mm PVC, 560 mm, 23 g, tie-wrapped at (0.164, 0.283), 5.8 mm above the table. The tie-wraps grip firmly: a 15 N pull draws a cable 5 mm through. Both cables leave the plate along -y for 20 mm, turn 30 deg toward the robot (grey for 80 mm, orange for 120 mm) and then lie straight on the table parallel to the carrier on the robot's side: grey at x=0.136 to its end at y=-0.266, orange at x=0.104 to y=-0.261. Cable bending: a 100 mm overhang droops about 15 mm (grey) and 17 mm (orange). Friction: carrier 0.30/0.25, cables 0.45/0.35. Full dimension and parts tables: README.
scoring: End state, measured on the carrier and the two cables. Link k is covered when, over the middle 24 mm of the link, both cables lie inside the channel (each cable's centre within its own radius + 1.5 mm of the inner side plates, below the crossbar line and down on the bottom crossbars within 2 mm) and the link's crossbar is LATCHED: swung shut to within 2.5 deg (its free end at most 1.4 mm proud of the side plate) with the catch snapped back over it (within 0.5 mm of its rest position). Score = 0.05 per covered link (up to 0.6); + 0.2 if both cables lie inside all twelve links without crossing (grey's centre at least 1 mm farther from the robot than orange's at every 5 mm along the carrier); + 0.2 if all twelve links are covered and both cable ends come out at least 60 mm past the moving end. Every credit also needs both grippers released (each gripper's centre point at least 30 mm from the bounding boxes of the carrier and of both cables) and everything at rest (cable points moving under 0.5 mm and crossbars under 0.25 deg per 50 ms step), held for 1 s; otherwise 0. A crossbar resting on its catch, or shut on a cable riding a side plate, is not latched; a link with only one cable inside earns nothing; crossbars shut over an empty carrier earn nothing. Permanent 0 for the rest of the trial (sticky, checked every step): either cable is ever pulled more than 5 mm through its tie-wrap (strain relief torn). Success = 1.0 held 1 s. Real trial: after the robot lets go, lay a straightedge across each crossbar's side plates (a latched bar is flush, an unlatched one rests on its catch 4.1 mm proud) and lift each bar's free end with a fingernail (a latched bar does not come up); take a top photo: the cables show through the 20 mm gaps between crossbars, so their order and whether both are inside are read link by link; measure the cable ends past the moving end with a ruler; a tape mark at each tie-wrap shows any slip.
run_limit: 3,600 steps (180 s at 20 Hz); the scripted demo reaches success at step 1,274 (64 s)
reset_notes: Press each catch back with a fingernail and swing all twelve crossbars open onto their stops; pull both cables out and lay them on the table beside the carrier on the robot's side, each leaving its tie-wrap straight and turning toward the robot at 30 degrees (grey for 80 mm, orange for 120 mm) before running parallel to the chain. Check that neither cable has slipped in its tie-wrap (tape mark at the tie).
fidelity: The carrier lies straight, openable side up, as for filling; its links are then on their straight stops and the bench, so it is one rigid body (link pivots not modelled). Each crossbar is rigid on a hinge; its moulded snap lug is a sprung catch (300 N/m, 45 deg lead-in) set to about 3 N at the free end: measure your chain's. Cables are 20 mm rigid capsule segments with bending springs, no twist; the tie-wrap is a stiff axial spring (15 N draws the cable 5 mm, counted as torn out).
